Do you use iTunes? Bandcamp? Spotify?

I'm an old bastard. Close to fifty. I remember being a teen a living in a record store. Nothing better than browsing the stacks for bands I had never heard of.

In the nineties I went digital. Had numerous hard drives at work I filled with tracks. Ripped all of my CDs. 300 gig worth. That was a great deal back then.

New releases I would buy, until DRM issues made be pissed. I admit I stole more than I should have.

Today it's Spotify. I love it. I share songs and albums with friends. I find new things I never imagined I would have liked.

I have a subscription to Google Play All Access which isnjust their streaming service. I normally just listen to shit I already know on there and sometimes play one of their radio stations. Honestly, if I had more time in the day, or a Bluetooth connection in my car, I would play their stations a lot more. They have good unthemed stations that can generally give you some more obscure tracks. Granted they may not be hidden gems, but they definitely are good background music.

Besides that I buy records from time to time of my favorite albums just to have a physical copy of it. Sometimes I'll raid the used section and pick up things I've never heard of but more often than not I stick with what I know.

I'm 22 and If I want to listen to music on the go digitally, I use Spotify Premium. It's really awesome since I can just look up an artist I like and listen to their discography without resorting to piracy. Before Spotify, I resorted to downloading music and syncing it with my Zune HD(It still works), but now I rarely download. The only reason I download is if a band I like doesn't release their material on Spotify (King Crimson for example) or if what I'm looking for is really rare and unavailable (some Goa Trance tracks), but again that's rare.

Now for physical copies, I only buy vinyl records for albums that are really worthy of listening to on a turntable (Can, Aphex Twin, Neu!, Joy Division). I would spend almost a hundred bucks on three records, but it's totally worth it in the end. Sometimes, I buy some random house/techno/breakbeat record for 2 bucks, but it's a fun mix bag to have.

I am 27 and I am in love with Google Play All Access.

Honestly I dreaded the idea of not owning the music I listen to. I've been on the internet for..a while. And of all the things I've adapted to, giving up true ownership of music was just one of the things I wasn't willing to relinquish.

Then the Google overlords came and with their takeover and integration of almost everything I'm plugged into. I could not help but bump into Google Play. This happened on my android phone and so I tried it out for 30 days and just..wow.

Easiest way to explain it, for me, is that I got tired of pirating. Not that it wasn't easy but it just wasn't as instantly fulfilling. As my taste grew and got more obscure I found I spent more time/effort searching for things for free than just buying it (online or at actual stores).

And with GP I found true freedom in a way I hadn't had before. I found a seemingly endless well of bands and music to explore, at my fingertips and ready on demand. I didn't have to hope amazon had it, search 50 sites to find a torrent, or even leave my house.

And beyond the lazy factor I've discovered so many bands my whole list of artists I want to see has completely changed. I have a literal arsenal of bands I'd never have had a chance to experience that I now want to throw my money at and would LOVE LOVE LOVE to see and support. And I can't say that my 10 bucks I throw in the well per month for GP goes or helps them but I like to think it's doing more than pirating did.

Also I have a rare job that for 97% of the time I'm at work I can listen to my own music in my headphones and the fact Google Play allows me download the music on my phone to listen to offline so I don't have to kill my data plan while still being able to have fresh music is a huge plus.
My pleasure! Hope to contribute here more some day :)
